blocks.text: Carmen, Frasquita, Mercedes, the Officer, Morales, other Officers, Gipsies, &c.
The Tavern of Lillas Pastia. Benches right and left. Towards the end of a dinner. The table is in confusion.

Frasquita, Mercedes, the Officer, Morales, are with Carmen. The Officers are smoking. Two Gipsies in a corner play the Guitar, and two others dance. Carmen looks at them. The Officer speaks to her, she does not listen to him, but suddenly rises and sings.

lines: Ah! when of gay guitars the sound
On the air in cadence ringing,
To dance a merry, mazy round.
In rhythm with the music beating,
And ev’ry voice is heard repeating
The merry burthen of our glad song. Tra la la la.

blocks.text: During the burthen of the song, the Gipsies dance, Mercedes and Frasquita sing “Tra la la” with Carmen.

lines: Cheeks now flush and jewels shine,
Scarves are floating to the wind;
Round and round in merry maze
So the dance and song unite,
From measure slow to fastest strain;
As the strings the gipsies sweep,
Yet a wilder dance is on—
And here, whilst floats around the song—
Alas! find reason lost at last.

blocks.text: Moment of rapid and violent dance. Carmen also commences to dance, and as the last notes sound, unable to continue, falls on a seat near at hand.

lines: What does Master Pastia want of us now?
He tells me the chief Corregidor
Desires him to shut up the inn.
And thou, Carmen, art thou not coming?
About the soldier I put in prison,
Through thee, the other day—in prison,
From which he has only to-day been released.

blocks.text: The scene is interrupted by a song in the distance.
The Officer goes to the window.

lines: He looks like the victor of the circus in Granada.
We shall be pleased to drink your health, comrade,
With you to drink will be a pleasure,
Should Toreadors go side by side;
Crowded the Circus on a festival day,
Crowded the Circus from floor to roof,
Wild with excitement the populace are.
Each one among them of you is speaking—
All are shouting till the combat is over,
Because ’tis a festival rare of its kind.
Do not forget the brightest of eyes!
Yes, love’s the prize waits thee, oh, Toreador.

blocks.text: Between the verses Carmen fills Escamillo’s glass.

lines: At last each one is hushed to silence.
What has happened? what is this?
Forth the bull comes in his fury,
Already pierced through a horse has fallen,
Bravo, bull! the mob are shrieking!
He goes, he comes, he rushes on,
And tries to tear the bandrol down;
And now with blood the ring is full;

blocks.text: All drink, and clasp hands with the Toreador. The Officers get ready to go. Escamillo draws near Carmen.

lines: Maiden, say what art thou called?
In peril I would invoke thy name.
Carmen, or Carmencita, each one calls me.
And if one—if one might say he loved you?
I should say that he must not.
Too amiable Carmen does not appear;
But I am content to hope—to wait.
To wait you are permitted, and ’tis sweet to hope.
Since you will not come, Carmen, I shall return.
’Twill be in vain if you do.
That may be, but I’ll try.

blocks.text: All but the three Zingarelle leave the scene.
Lillas Pastia closes the shutters and goes out.

lines: Perhaps we may yet strike out some plan:
But it is necessary for you to be with us.
We have a fine business in view.
Profitable? or, at least, said to be?
Really; we the truth you tell,
When there’s a question of cheating,
The women must be of the party;
The attempt goes for nothing, or worse.
Ah! the attempt goes for nothing,
Where there’s a question of cheating, etc.
But, at so short a notice—
If to leave it suits you, be it so;
But I shall not go on this journey,
Here shall I stay—I shall not depart.
Thou will not let us set off
Here shall I stay—I will not go.
But at least tell us the reason why, Carmen.
I will tell you why, sincerely,—
The reason is in my heart—
Come, Carmen, this is a serious thing.
I am in love, seriously, and go not.
The thing is certain and extraordinary.
And well to thee, loving fair one—
That duty and love should go together.
Dear sirs, I should be happy to set off
But I am not free to follow you;
Duty must give place to love.
Then thou wilt not come with us?
Ah, Carmen, come; you must come.
For this affair, with us to stay:
’Tis true, ’tis true; the reason’s to me known.
Where there’s a question of cheating, &c.
Who the other day for kindness to me
Are you sure he will come!
Stay and listen! He is here already.

blocks.text: Don Jose’s voice is heard in the distance.

lines: Faith, he would make a good smuggler.

blocks.text: Il Remendado signs to the others to leave Carmen alone. They all go out.
advancing, but still in the distance

lines: Where love of beauty calls me.
And they put thee in prison?
For two months I was there.
If ’twould serve thee, I would stay there yet.
The officers were here a short time since,
May I die if he is not jealous!
I will dance for thy pleasure,
And thou shalt see how Carmen

blocks.text: Makes Jose sit in a corner, and dances, accompanying herself with castanets. Jose’s eyes are fixed on her, fascinated. The recall is heard in the distance. Jose starts up and goes to Carmen.

lines: It seemed to me down yonder—
Yes, ’tis the trumpet sounding the retreat;
Really? I am very glad of it.
It must have been music in the air.

blocks.text: Begins to dance again. The call draws nearer and passes beneath the window, then dies away in the distance. Jose takes Carmen’s arm and obliges her to cease.

lines: That sound orders me to return to quarters?
Recall to quarters? I am a fool indeed!
To divert you with my dance.
I thought—Heaven pardon me!—he loved me;
And the trumpet sounds his recall!

blocks.text: Throws his cap, &c., with rage at him.

lines: There! thy cap, thy sabre, thy pouch!
And go directly to the barracks!
Carmen, thou art wrong thus to jest.
’Tis hard to part, for in my heart
Felt greater ardor, warmer love for thee!
Ta, ta, ta, ta! Great heaven!—the recall!
Ta, ta, ta, ta! I must return.
His head is turned: and this is his love.
Then such love thou believest not?
Go: I will not punish thee.
Thou must listen to me, Carmen; I desire it.

blocks.text: With his left hand he holds Carmen’s arm, and with his right opens his uniform and takes out the flowers she gave him in the first Act.

lines: The flowers once to me you gave,
Within my prison have I cherish’d;
For me still perfume they retain’d,
Though all their beauty long had perish’d.
Night and day, in dungeon gloomy,
Carmen, I swear I thought of thee:
And while their fragrance fill’d my brain,
Thy name invoked, so far from me.
My fatal love for thee I curs’d,
And I regretted in my wrath
That brought thy form across my path.
Ah! horror held me for its own,
And one sad thought filled heart and brain,
That I might see thee once again.
Now but one tender glance I ask,
One word of kindness from thee crave:
True my heart to thine is ever;
Carmen, am I not thy slave?
No; if thou didst love me,
On thy horse would we ride,
O’er the vast plains we’d traverse,
If thou didst love me a little.
Together up yonder would we go;
No captain forced then to obey,
No more the trumpet wouldst thou hear
For roof, the sky—a wandering life;
And above all—most prized of all—
Up yonder, up yonder, if thou lov’st me,
Up yonder, up yonder, together we’ll go.
Up yonder, up yonder, thus will we go
Away, if thou lov’st me, together.
No, I must not listen to thee,
No; no longer do I love you; I hate you!
Farewell! Never will I see you again.

blocks.text: Turns towards the door. At this moment a knocking is heard.

lines: The choice does not do you honor;
Prefer a soldier to his officer!
Will you go about your business?
Infernal! thy blood for this shall pay!

blocks.text: Il Dancairo, Il Remendado, and the Gipsies enter from different sides. Carmen points to the Officer. Il Dancairo and Remendado seize him.

lines: Love an ugly trick has played you.
We from this inn must go soon;
Will you or will you not?
Resistance is vain, and I must yield;
But I shall know how to punish you.
And it is your turn now, my gay captain.
May it please you march, without more words.

blocks.text: The Officer goes between four Gipsies with pistols levelled at him.

lines: And wilt thou now come with us?
Thou wilt be glad when thou seest
How pleasant is this wandering life,—
Our will the law—and, above all,
The heaven over all—the wandering life—
Our will the law—and, above all,
